subject: Post‑Incident Readout: Distributed KV drift — findings, timeline, and commitments
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finovate.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post‑Incident Readout: Distributed KV drift — findings, timeline, and commitments

Elena / Tom,

Thank you for your patience while our team completed the initial investigation into yesterday's service anomalies that affected some inference sessions on your dedicated pool. I wanted to share a concise, customer-facing readout and our immediate commitments — attached are the timeline and the mitigation checklist for your verification.

What happened (summary):
- Between 03:12 and 03:52 UTC we observed inconsistent KV-store state across a subset of GPUs servicing your dedicated capacity, which led to stale prefix cache hits and out-of-order session tokens for ~1.7% of requests routed to that pool.
- Symptom: elevated token duplication and occasional session desynchronization for multi-turn chat workloads (we saw retries and truncated outputs for a narrow set of request sizes).

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a control-plane race during a rolling metadata propagation step after a small config migration. Under specific timing we had a window where KV routing tables were partially applied, causing some replicas to serve from an older cache namespace.

Impact to Finovate: partial request degradation (latency and incorrect continuation) for the affected time window; no customer data exfiltration detected.

Immediate actions we took:
- Stopped the in-flight propagation and ran coordinated reconciliation to restore consistent KV namespaces.
- Rolled a hotfix to the metadata propagation code to serialize the migration step for affected clusters.
- Deployed additional validation checks that abort a migration on any namespace divergence.

Next steps / commitments to you:
1) Final RCA and timeline (attached PDF) by EOD Monday with evidence artifacts and validation logs.
2) Patch verification: we will run a broadened canary across your dedicated pool and provide per-shard verification results by Nov 2nd.
3) Compensatory review: our account team will propose SLA credit options if the incident meets the threshold in your contract.
4) Hardening: we will add a pre-migration dry-run, stronger reconciliation checks, and an alert rule to detect propagation inconsistencies.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: kv-drift-timeline.pdf (PDF, 120KB)], [Attachment: mitigation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)].

Would you like a technical readout call to walk through the timeline and logs tomorrow or early next week? If so, propose a window and we'll confirm.

Apologies for the disruption — we know predictability is critical for Finovate. We'll own the follow-through and keep you updated frequently.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@finovate.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@finovate.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post‑Incident Readout: Distributed KV drift — findings, timeline, and commitments

David,

Thank you for the prompt update and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying questions:
- Can you confirm whether any user sessions were definitively lost or corrupted (we need a clear yes/no for our internal audit)?
- When you say "no data exfiltration detected," are you referring to customer payloads only, or also metadata and audit logs?
- Regarding SLA credits, we'd like an initial estimate of compensation range so our procurement team can prepare.

We'd like to schedule a readout call — availability tomorrow (Oct 31) between 10:00–12:00 ET or Monday (Nov 2) in the morning ET. Please confirm which works and include any engineers who will cover the log walk-through.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Platform Reliability
Finovate Financial

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finovate.com>, Tom Baxter <tbaxter@finovate.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Readout call notes, evidence links, and action owners

Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for joining the readout this morning. Per our call, summary and concrete commitments below — full artifacts are attached and we’ve posted evidence to the internal drive links in the metadata.

Confirmed facts:
- No customer payloads were exported from our systems. Our forensics review shows no unusual outbound network flows correlated to the incident window.
- We did observe partial namespace divergence in the metadata propagation path; that divergence caused 1.7% of requests routed against stale KV namespaces. Those requests could return repeated tokens or truncated continuations but were not returned to other tenants.
- Affected sessions: we identified 4,279 unique session IDs in Finovate's pool that had the symptoms during the 40-minute window. We will provide the session list in a secure artifact for your audit team.

Action items and owners (target dates):
- Marcus Lin: Per-shard verification report and reconciliation logs (deliverable: 2026-11-03T23:59:00Z).
- Hannah Schmitt: Post-migration validation gating added to the control plane and alert rule published (done — gating completed; alert rule in INF-4721, verification by 2026-11-05).
- Priya Natarajan (Billing): SLA credit proposal and statement of impact (deliverable: 2026-11-04).
- Engineering: Canary dry-run across a mirrored subset of your pool (scheduled: 2026-11-02 14:00–16:00 ET; rollback criteria documented in mitigation-checklist.xlsx).

Customer verification steps: please use the attached checklist to validate behavior in your staging mirror; we will coordinate a joint verification run and share the acceptance report.

Attachments: [kv-drift-timeline.pdf], [mitigation-checklist.xlsx]

We take responsibility for the regression and will follow through on the delivery commitments above. If you need any further breakdowns (per-request logs, session traces), reply to this thread and we will prioritize.

Best regards,
David Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
